affected_party: QIF evaluators, judge-policy owners, and stakeholders affected by automated or hybrid judgments
actual_problem: QIF can replay policy routes, but cannot determine whether a judge changes its classification when identical evidence is paired with different downstream-use or consequence framing, nor whether an available abstain route produces justified uncertainty rather than refusal or malformed output.
why_it_matters: A judge may appear accurate while allowing anticipated downstream effects to distort measurement, and aggregate accuracy can hide whether abstention is useful, excessive, or confused with failure.
why_now: v0.6.40 established identical-evidence counterfactual replay; current evidence shows consequential framing can induce motivated mislabeling and that abstain options do not eliminate incorrect labels.
